Visit note | 2025-11-16 03:00 PM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Hossain Matubbar, 52, male. Mr. Matubbar presents with chest tightness when walking fast or climbing, noting a heavy feeling in the chest that eases with rest within minutes, alongside breathlessness on effort. He states this started while carrying shopping bags uphill in Tongi. He works as a madrasa teacher, is married, and has a smoking history of ten cigarettes daily. He has Hypothyroidism. He denies orthopnoea or palpitations at rest. On examination: BP 153/88 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 59 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no murmurs, and lung bases are clear. Assessment: Stable angina. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid heavy exertion until review, walk 20 minutes daily on flat ground, and stop smoking. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and fasting lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-11-16 03:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Riad Mondal, 56, male. Mr. Mondal reports coughing at night, a tight chest in dust or cold air, and occasional wheezing. He mentions these symptoms flared during the winter smog in Mymensingh. He is employed as a bank officer and is a non-smoker with no reported chronic comorbidities. He denies fever or unexplained weight loss. On examination: SpO2 92%, BP 131/78 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 94 kg. Chest auscultation reveals widespread expiratory wheezes bilaterally. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep the bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-11-16 03:00 PM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Shamim Islam, 52, male. Mr. Islam attends for review concerning gritty burning eyes, long hours of screen time, and symptoms that are worse in air conditioning. He notes his complaints began after long gaming sessions at home in Faridpur. He works as a hotel receptionist and has no systemic comorbidity. He denies any sudden loss of vision or eye discharge. On examination: tear break-up time 5 seconds, BP 129/80 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 52 kg. Conjunctivae show mild dryness without injection. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-11-16 04:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Chandana Sarkar, 62, female. Mrs. Sarkar describes severe aching in her bones and muscles, pain behind her eyes, and a sudden high fever that started after a week of stagnant rainwater around the house in Rampura. She works as a madrasa teacher and has a history of Bronchial asthma. She reports no urinary symptoms or cough. On examination: platelet count 83000 per microlitre, temperature 101.5°F, BP 133/75 mmHg, pulse 94 bpm, weight 89 kg. Chest is clear on auscultation. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.
